description: Takes a video and a description of what to change and generates the SAME clip with those changes applied (different characters, clothes, setting) while the camera move, timing, framing and the performers' motion stay as they were. Returns the new job's id immediately. WHEN: the user wants to restyle, recast or reskin footage they already have ('make the crowd elderly', 'put them all in suits', 'make it snow'): the source decides what HAPPENS, the prompt what it LOOKS like. Not `generate_video` with a reference: nothing is invented from scratch. THE SOURCE CLIP MUST BE 3 TO 10 SECONDS: a longer one is REFUSED before anything is charged, so cut a long video into sub-10-second pieces (independent jobs, joined afterwards). Frame size and rate are resized and re-timed server-side, not refused. THE PROVIDER SCREENS THE SOURCE FOR REAL PEOPLE: footage of identifiable real people (a music video, a film, a clip off the internet) can be refused as a likeness, and a refused job is REFUNDED in full; that is a property of the footage, so rewording does not help. THE CARD: this call already opened the aicut card: do not call `show_generation` for this job. WAIT: `wait_for_generation` (this id, `media`), again at once while `terminal: false`, then one short line; no `get_*` polling, timers, background shells or narrating the wait. No card? Give the user the `url`. COST: this spends the user's tokens: a per-second rate that depends on resolution times the LENGTH, the SOURCE clip's by default (1080p costs more; a 10-second clip costs about three times a 3-second one). The clip's length is MEASURED BY THE SERVER: that measurement is the price. A clip it cannot measure (a WebM, an unreadable header) is REFUSED uncharged: re-encode to MP4. With `reference_images`, a `duration` you send IS what is priced. REFERENCE IMAGES (optional) steer the result with up to a few pictures (a face, an outfit, a prop); the source still decides motion, timing and camera. Sending any switches on a second provider mode that also accepts `duration` (otherwise the source's length) and `aspect_ratio` (otherwise inherited): set either only when the user asked. An external url costs one media-ingest slot: quote and create from the SAME url to pay it once. SPENDS TOKENS: price with `estimate_only: true`, ask in the SAME message as the price, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase (SPENDING RULES, this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: a reused `idempotency_key` REPLAYS the first job whatever the settings: never reuse one for a new generation (this server's instructions).

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio (for example `9:16`); only meaningful with `reference_images` (otherwise inherited from the source clip). Only if the user asked; never to save tokens, never carried over.

duration.description: Output length in seconds; only meaningful with `reference_images` (otherwise the source clip's own length). Only if the user asked; never to save tokens, never carried over.

prompt.description: What to CHANGE about the clip: describe the replacement, not the whole scene (the camera, timing and motion are kept, so directions about them are wasted). Name what each thing in frame becomes.

reference_images.description: URLs of up to a few images to steer the result (a face, an outfit, a prop). Same URL rules as `source_video`. Sending this switches to kling-o3's `references` mode, which also accepts `duration` and `aspect_ratio`; omit it for a plain edit.

resolution.description: Output resolution; 1080p costs more per second. REQUIRED: use `720p` unless the user asked for `1080p`, and name the choice in the priced ask; never carried over from an earlier request.

source_video.description: URL of the video to edit, 3 to 10 seconds long. A URL from this account's generations or uploads, or a public https URL (imported first); another account's is refused.

name: edit_video
title: Rewrite what is in a video, keeping its motion
